open_items: ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: fifth occurrence, cycles 150-152 (3 consecutive cycles, 4 hours), resolved by cycle 153, healthy through cycle 160 (no new occurrence, 9 consecutive healthy cycles). Longest occurrence yet (prior max was 2 consecutive cycles, cycles 150-151; before that all resolved within one cycle: cycle 26, cycle 134, cycle 143). Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py). Watch for a sixth occurrence; if it spans 4+ cycles, treat as a genuine regression rather than the known cosmetic pattern.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: ninth episode (cycles 144-145) resolved by cycle 146, clean through cycle 160 (15 consecutive healthy cycles). No fix applied under docs-only scope; standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) carried forward for a session with code-change scope. Watch for a tenth episode, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle or two.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 160: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests, seen on ABS, OECD, ILO, and FBOS. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.

ILO direct-path 403 flap: third occurrence at cycle 159 (10:01:22Z), broadest yet - 10 of 12 contract assertions broken (auth:listing, constraint:availableconstraint, errors:missing_artefact, and all seven references:* checks), resolved by cycle 160. Prior occurrences: cycle 32 (data+json only), cycle 94 (metadata+data+json plus 4 contract assertions). All three resolved within one cycle. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout cycle 159 - only contract-probe traffic drew the 403, suggesting a rate-limit/WAF trip against probe volume rather than a general ILO outage. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect this - it showed healthy/[] for ILO at cycle 159 despite the cycle being degraded. Future runs must check /api/contracts changes and /api/cycle/{id} for intermediate cycles, not rely on /api/history alone. Watch for a fourth occurrence, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 429 flap at cycle 126 (direct data + direct json), resolved by cycle 127, still resolved through cycle 160 (33 more cycles clean). Watch for recurrence; a second episode soon would suggest rate-limit triggering rather than a one-off.
